title: Berkshire 2025 annual meeting: Buffett on patience, float, currency risk, and handing the reins to Greg Abel
summary: Buffett's last meeting as CEO, where he announces Greg Abel will take over at year end. He explains why he holds $335B in cash, why markets demand emotional control, why he distrusts currency debasement and earnings management, and what makes Berkshire's insurance float unique.

principles.text: Great opportunities arrive irregularly, so stay liquid and patient rather than forcing capital out on a schedule.
principles.quote: Things get extraordinarily attractive very occasionally.

principles.text: Investors must control their emotions; the market will not adapt to you, so you must adapt to it.
principles.quote: the world is not going to adapt to you. You're going to have to adapt to the world.

principles.text: Governments tend to debase currency over time, which is a core long-term risk to guard against.
principles.quote: the tendency of a government to want to debase its currency over time is there's no system that beats that.

principles.text: Surround yourself with people better than you, because you drift toward the company you keep.
principles.quote: you want to hang out with people that are better than you are

principles.text: Study balance sheets over many years before income statements, since they are harder to manipulate.
principles.quote: I spend more time looking at balance sheets than I do income statements.

principles.text: Don't make decisions to manage reported quarterly or annual earnings; focusing on a number tempts people to play games.
principles.quote: we don't do anything based on its impact on quarterly and annual earnings.
